The final packed candidate imported three public issues and passed its Node repeat, privacy gate, and strict health. Keep this separate from passing Node workflow safety and from the all-source coverage blocker.

value.text: The final packed candidate matched all three authored runtime modules byte-for-byte. Its fresh Node public import passed with three issues, a byte-identical second run, zero gate findings, and strict health in 24.94 seconds. value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Packed installed-CLI reproduction with the pinned host passes three consecutive native Bun repeats under the unchanged 45-second watchdog. The complete fixture test took 26.63 seconds, including packing, installation, Node import, and all three repeats; each retained item bytes and unchanged bare-remote refs. Separately reproduced a real dangling comment-lock symlink: open with exclusive creation returns EEXIST while stat returns ENOENT, causing the old immediate-continue path to busy-spin forever. The preserved fix adds sleep and checks the existing wait budget. This is a proven local lock defect, not yet proof of the historical installed-host timeout cause. Further public-data and diagnostic acceptance follows.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Acceptance now uses a shared process-group watchdog: the original 45-second deadline sends SIGTERM, then a separate five-second cleanup window sends SIGKILL. A timed-out command is always rejected, even if it exits zero afterward, and no writer step follows. The deterministic negative control uses a real CPU-spinning child that ignores SIGTERM; the watchdog force-kills it with unchanged durable fixture bytes. This bounds the historical installed-host timeout without claiming the dangling-lock defect was its original cause or increasing the execution deadline. The CLI lock defect itself now honors its existing wait budget.

patch.value: The intermittent historical installed-Bun repeat has not reproduced in three fresh packed repeats and three live-public-snapshot repeats. A real dangling comment-lock symlink independently reproduced an unbounded busy loop, fixed by honoring the existing wait budget. Installed acceptance retains its 45-second execution deadline and now force-kills the process group after a separate five-second cleanup window; timeout always fails even on a later zero exit. Recent repeats preserve durable bytes and strict health. The historical root cause remains unestablished.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Native Bun full-suite negative control found a real HTTP boundary failure: a local server accepts the connection and never responds; requestOnce relies on ClientRequest.setTimeout(30000), but under installed Bun 1.3.5 no timeout rejection arrives before the existing 45-second test deadline. The identical full Node case passes. A fresh focused native reproduction is running. Stopped the superseded Bun release check so the transport fix can be verified on frozen source. This is an independently observed request-timeout defect, not proof of the historical public repeat cause.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Focused native Bun before-fix reproduction fails deterministically: one local silent-server test reaches 45.00 seconds without the 30-second socket-timeout rejection (38 unrelated tests filtered). Replacing reliance on ClientRequest.setTimeout with an explicit 30-second wall-clock timer, cleared on Promise settlement; the timer destroys the request and rejects directly. Regression now exercises two real responses concurrently: no headers, and headers plus a partial body that never completes. No execution deadline or test timeout was raised. Node and native Bun focused validation is underway.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The expanded native regression also caught a second concrete behavior: destroying a partial-response request before rejecting can synchronously emit response end under Bun, resolving the incomplete response instead of rejecting. The deadline callback now rejects first, then destroys. The real silent-server and never-ending partial-body cases test that ordering at the original 30-second limit. Node passes the expanded case; final native focused run and complete gates are being reverified. These are transport-boundary observations, not an assertion about the historical public-data repeat.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: After-fix focused real-HTTP regression PASS under both runtimes: Node 30.02 seconds, native Bun 30.02 seconds; both silent headers and partial never-ending body reject with the expected 30-second timeout. The test keeps its 45-second harness deadline and asserts completion below 40 seconds. Build:test and ESLint pass. Explicit deadline rejection precedes destroy and its timer is cleared on every Promise settlement. Restarting full npm release checks and all native Bun files on this frozen fix.

value.text: Investigating PR #108 clone-only workflow setup failures. Plan: reproduce in a scratch clone, trace the npm lifecycle trigger and Git layout difference, isolate package preparation from the fixture tracker, then verify regression and full release gates in both layouts.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Reproduced the reported failure in a fresh clone with Node 22 and npm 10.9.8 after building. The failing command is npm pack --ignore-scripts in prepareWorkflowFixture, before pm package install. npm 10 pacote runs prepare despite ignore-scripts; npm 11 checks ignoreScripts and the same clone passes. The fixture passes its external PM_PATH into the package-root hook. Testing the worktree with npm 10 to verify whether Git layout is causal.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Confirmed npm 10 also fails in the package worktree with an external PM_PATH; Git layout and preinstalled merge drivers are not causal. The fix binds package packing to the package-local tracker and leaves caller import commands on their fixture tracker. Added a regression that forces the real prepare hook before packing in a fresh clone and a linked worktree, so npm 11 cannot mask the bug. The reusable caller workflow does not pack this source checkout and its npm ci/merge install run with its own repository tracker.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Regression verified red/green: removing only the package-local PM_PATH override fails with the reported outside-repository error; restoring it passes. pm test pm-github-hptv --run --match 'workflow packing isolates' --progress passed. ESLint and test TypeScript build passed. Running all three originally failing acceptance tests plus the layout regression under npm 10 in the worktree before pushing.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Both layout regressions fail on reverting the PM_PATH override, including the linked worktree with the pinned CLI. npm 10 exposed a second packing detail after fixing the root mismatch: successful prepare stdout contaminates npm pack --json by default. Packing now explicitly uses --foreground-scripts=false to preserve the JSON receipt; the regression also supplies a conflicting inherited foreground-scripts setting.
